League
LEEG
n.
From Old French ligue, from Latin ligare, to bind. Webster 1828: an alliance or confederacy between princes or states for their mutual aid or defence. In the Authorized Version it names a binding political covenant — one that Israel was forbidden to make with the Canaanites and did make anyway, once, by deception.

Biblical Definition

A league in Scripture is a sworn alliance, and the Old Testament treats it as a matter of covenant loyalty rather than diplomacy. The command was flat: ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land; ye shall throw down their altars: but ye have not obeyed my voice (Judges 2:2). The Gibeonites therefore came disguised: We be come from a far country: now therefore make ye a league with us (Joshua 9:6). Israel’s error is recorded in the next verses — they asked the right question, Peradventure ye dwell among us; and how shall we make a league with you? (Joshua 9:7), and then failed to ask the LORD. Joshua made peace with them, and made a league with them, to let them live: and the princes of the congregation sware unto them (Joshua 9:15). The oath, once sworn, bound Israel for centuries, and God later avenged its breach by Saul. Not every league is forbidden: David made a league with them in Hebron before the LORD (2 Samuel 5:3), and Hiram and Solomon made a league together (1 Kings 5:12). The distinction is not between alliance and isolation but between an alliance that serves the covenant and one that binds God’s people to those whose altars they were commanded to throw down.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines LEAGUE as an alliance or confederacy between princes or states for their mutual aid or defence; and a combination or union of two or more parties for the maintenance of friendship or the prosecution of a common design.

expand to see more

LEAGUE, n. [Fr. ligue; L. ligo, to bind.] — An alliance or confederacy between princes or states for their mutual aid or defence.

A combination or union of two or more parties for the maintenance of friendship and mutual interest, or for the prosecution of some design.

LEAGUE, v.i. — To unite or confederate, as princes or states.

The Latin root is to bind, and that is the biblical weight. Joshua 9 turns on the fact that a sworn league binds even when it was entered by mistake, because the oath was sworn before the LORD.

Key Scripture

Joshua 9:6 — "And they went to Joshua unto the camp at Gilgal, and said unto him, and to the men of Israel, We be come from a far country: now therefore make ye a league with us."

Joshua 9:15 — "And Joshua made peace with them, and made a league with them, to let them live: and the princes of the congregation sware unto them."

Judges 2:2 — "And ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land; ye shall throw down their altars: but ye have not obeyed my voice: why have ye done this?"

2 Samuel 5:3 — "So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a league with them in Hebron before the LORD: and they anointed David king over Israel."

1 Kings 5:12 — "And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as he promised him: and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon; and they two made a league together."

Modern Corruption

The league is corrupted when the church enters binding alliances with those whose doctrine it is bound to oppose — the ecclesiastical version of Joshua 9 — and equally when a lawful alliance is treated as compromise and the church withdraws from every common cause.

expand to see more

Joshua 9 records the mechanism exactly. The Gibeonites do not argue Israel out of the command; they present a false account of who they are, with mouldy bread and cracked bottles, and Israel asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD (Joshua 9:14). The church makes the same mistake when it enters formal partnership with bodies whose confession it has not examined, on the strength of a shared cause and a friendly presentation. Ecumenical agreements that treat the Reformation’s doctrinal issues as settled or secondary are Gibeonite leagues: the terms are sworn before the question is asked. Paul’s rule for the church is not diplomatic but plain — come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord (2 Corinthians 6:17).

The opposite error must also be named, since Scripture records leagues God did not condemn. David’s covenant with the elders at Hebron was made before the LORD, and Solomon’s treaty with Hiram supplied the timber for the temple. Christians may join with unbelievers in civil work, trade, and the ordinary business of a shared society without sinning; the second commandment does not forbid a contract. The line falls where the alliance requires the church to leave altars standing that God commanded thrown down — that is, where the price of the league is the silencing of the church’s testimony.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The Hebrew word is berith, the ordinary word for covenant; the KJV renders it league where the parties are political and covenant where God is a party. The distinction is the translators’ and it is a useful one.

expand to see more

Hebrew berith (H1285) — a covenant, treaty, alliance; rendered league in Joshua 9:6, Judges 2:2, 2 Samuel 5:3, and 1 Kings 5:12.

The KJV’s choice of league for human-to-human treaties and covenant where God is a party is a translators’ convention, not a distinction in the Hebrew.

Hebrew karath berith — literally to cut a covenant, from the divided animals of Genesis 15; the same idiom underlies every league in these texts.

Hebrew shaba' (H7650) — to swear; the princes of the congregation sware unto them (Joshua 9:15) is what made the Gibeonite league unbreakable.

2 Samuel 21 records God’s judgment on Israel for Saul’s breach of that oath four centuries later — the measure of how binding a sworn league is.

Usage

"Ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land (Judges 2:2) — the command, with the charge of disobedience attached in the same verse."

"Made a league with them, to let them live (Joshua 9:15) — sworn without asking counsel of the LORD, and binding thereafter."

"King David made a league with them in Hebron before the LORD (2 Samuel 5:3) — a lawful covenant, made in God’s presence."
